findings.detail: D1 [verdict; CL10; counterarguments[0]; correctedUserAssumptions[2]] The draft says locking in the price has no value, which is stated too absolutely. That only holds if the price being locked is list price and the incumbent's renewal price stays at or below $14,700/month. The draft admits elsewhere that the 2027-03-01 renewal price is unknown (G3, tradeoff 3, furtherResearch item 2). It also allows that a negotiated Lumen rate may exist (CL6). If the lock covers a discounted rate, or the incumbent raises its price sharply at renewal, a lock could be worth something. 'Little or nothing is lost' (tradeoffs) is the defensible wording. 'Has no value' (verdict, CL10, correctedUserAssumptions) is not.

D2 [C3 assessment; CL9; K15; K17; alternatives[1]] The overlap range of 2 to 4 months (E7, K14-K17, CL9, C3) is taken from the packet without checking the dates. Today is 2026-11-11. If quarter end means 2026-12-31, signing then and starting to pay Lumen would give about 2 months of overlap before 2027-03-01. A 4-month overlap would need signing around 2026-11-01, which has already passed. So the upper bound ($47,600 overlap, $81,200 first-year premium) looks overstated. The draft also assumes without saying so that Lumen billing starts at signing rather than at go-live, and that the quarter is a calendar quarter.

D3 [alternatives[2]; furtherResearchThatCouldChangeConclusion[2]] The ingest-reduction alternative compares Lumen at 34 TB/month (11,900 / 350) against the incumbent's fixed $11,900. The option is labelled 'on either platform', but cutting ingest would probably lower the incumbent's cost too, and its pricing structure is unknown (G5). So 34 TB is not a valid break-even against the status quo. The same flaw appears in furtherResearchThatCouldChangeConclusion item 3.

D4 [edgeCasesAndFailureModes; counterarguments[2]; practicalImplications[1]] The draft never asks whether Lumen's billable 'GB ingested' is measured the same way as the usage report's 42 TB, for example raw versus compressed or after vendor-side processing. Vendors differ on this, and it is the one plausible way the vendor could defend a much smaller billable volume. The draft handles the TB/TiB question but not this one. It should be listed as an item to confirm in the written quote.

D5 [CL9] CL9 is marked material:false, but the overlap cost appears in the verdict ('before any months of paying both vendors') and is central to C3, the 15%-weighted contract-timing criterion. It should be flagged as material, or the verdict should not lean on it.

openDecisiveGaps: Will Lumen give a written, all-fees quote for 42,000 GB/month of logs plus traces, and what effective $/GB does it imply (break-even is about $0.2833/GB)?
What renewal price and termination/notice/auto-renewal terms does the incumbent contract set for 2027-03-01?
Does Lumen measure billable 'GB ingested' the same way the usage report measures the 42 TB (raw vs compressed, decimal vs binary)?
